newsitem.title: USA: OPTIONS - Dollar/mark, yen climb lifts options vols.
newsitem.headline: OPTIONS - Dollar/mark, yen climb lifts options vols.

text.p: The dollar's climb past the key 1.80 mark level and its approach of 116.00 yen bolstered implied volatilities further Tuesday as trade turned busy.
The U.S. unit stretched as high as 1.8040 marks at midmorning, its first foray above the perceived 1.80-mark barrier in nearly six years.
"Marks have been paid maybe as high as 11.2 in the one month and now the curve is probably 10.7/10.9 everything," said an OTC options broker.
The spot rise helped lift one-month dollar/mark to about 10.8 percent from 10.6 earlier Tuesday and also late Monday.

"When 1.80 traded there were a number of double-knockouts, reverse knockouts and digitals in the majors," he added. "But as far as I can see, the big (trade) in the options right now is the one-year dollar calls in dollar/yen."
Other brokers agreed that a hedge fund Monday and Tuesday bought as much as $7 billion total of one-year 10-delta, or 125-strike, yen puts, forcing shortcovering and boosting vols.
"I think that's what popped up the vols across the board," agreed another options broker of the 10-delta yen put trade.
"They (yen vols) are higher because of this interest that's gone on," said the first broker.
"Just supply and demand -- they're (market makers) all short and they had to buy stuff back," he added.
He quoted one-month yen at 10.6/10.9 percent, with one-year at 11.0/11.2, each about three-quarter point higher than Monday.

"The market was already short a lot of yen puts and it (dollar) went through a big technical level at 114.60, and combine that with Sakakibara's dollar-supportive comments last night and you have a prescription for a pretty good correction in dollar/yen and mark/yen," said a third OTC options broker.
Brokers also said the same hedge fund reportedly bought nearly $1 billion worth of six-month 1.5750 cable puts, adding pressure to spot sterling as well and hoisting vols upward.
One-month cable vols jumped to 10.0/10.4 percent, up sharply from 9.1/9.5 percent quoted near midday Monday.
"That's what caused some of the selloff in sterling," said the third options broker.
"The sterling and the yen were the ones (trades) everyone's talking about," added the first broker.
